verses.134:1: Louvai o nome do Senhor, * louvai, servos, o Senhor.
verses.134:2: {statis} de pé na casa do Senhor, * nos átrios da casa do nosso Deus.
verses.134:3: Louvai o Senhor, porque o Senhor é bom: * entoai salmos ao seu nome, porque é suave.
verses.134:4: Porque o Senhor escolheu para si Jacó, * Israel como sua posse.
verses.134:5: Porque {cognovi} que o Senhor é grande, * e o nosso Deus, acima de todos os deuses.
verses.134:6: Tudo o que quis, o Senhor fez no céu e na terra, * no mar e em todos os abismos.
verses.134:7a: {educens} as nuvens do extremo da terra: * {fulgura}.
verses.134:7b: {producit} {thesauris} os ventos: * {qui7b2} os primogênitos do Egito, desde o homem até o {pecus}.
verses.134:9: E enviou sinais e prodígios no meio de ti, Egito: * {pharao} todos os seus servos.
verses.134:10: {qui10} muitas nações: * e matou reis fortes:
verses.134:11: {sehon}, rei dos amorreus, e Og, rei de Basã, * e todos os reinos de Canaã.
verses.134:12: E deu a terra deles como herança, * como herança a Israel, o seu povo.
verses.134:13: Senhor, o vosso nome é para sempre: * Senhor, {memoriale}, de geração em geração.
verses.134:14: Porque o Senhor julgará o seu povo: * {deprec}.
verses.134:15: Os {simulacra} das nações são prata e ouro, * obras das mãos dos homens.
verses.134:16: Têm boca, e não falarão: * têm olhos, e não verão.
verses.134:18: {fiant} semelhantes a eles aqueles que os fazem: * e todos os que confiam neles.
verses.134:19: Casa de Israel, bendizei ao Senhor: * casa de Aarão, bendizei ao Senhor.
verses.134:20: Casa de Levi, bendizei ao Senhor: * vós que temeis o Senhor, bendizei ao Senhor.

decisions.why: 134:2 is 133:1b word for word, and the formula row (working) gives 'Que estais de pé na casa do Senhor'. Rule 6 asks identical Portuguese. But here the bare relative 'Que' opens the verse right after '… louvai, servos, o Senhor.', so the ear can hang it on 'o Senhor' (the Lord who stands in his house); and the Tuesday Lauds antiphon (Psalmi major, [Day2 Laudes1]) sings 134:1a and 134:2a as one line — 'Louvai o nome do Senhor, que estais de pé na casa do Senhor' would make the Lord the one standing. 'Vós que estais' names the addressees, as the vocative plural already implies (the Ps 10:2 remedy: the subject named). DRB 'You that stand', MS1932 'vós … que assistis'. Departure from the formula recorded; proposed for 133:1b too (glossary). Cost: two syllables over the Latin colon.

options.label: Vós que estais
options.note: Ruling. The addressees named, so the relative cannot attach to 'o Senhor', in the psalm or in the antiphon.

options.label: Que estais
options.note: 133:1b's wording, identical (the formula row). Heard after 'o Senhor', the relative can take the Lord as antecedent.

decisions.why: cognóvi + a 'that'-clause. v1 ruled 'eu soube' after 19:7a 'nunc cognóvi quóniam → agora soube que' and 55:10 'ecce, cognóvi → eis que eu soube'. Both the stylist and the ambiguity reader (v1) heard 'soube' as receiving news ('I found out, I heard'), not the settled knowledge of a confession. In 19:7a and 55:10 'nunc' and 'ecce' mark a moment, and 'soube' fits; here nothing does, and the Latin perfect of knowing states what is known (L&S; DRB 'I have known'). v2: 'eu sei' — the CNBB LH also has 'Eu bem sei que o Senhor é tão grande' (fetched, circulation.md; a witness of the ear only). The stylist's 'reconheci' is kept as an option: it is the cognate of recognóscere, and says acknowledgement more than knowledge.

options.label: eu sei
options.note: v2 ruling. The perfect's present sense; two readers refused 'soube'.

options.label: eu soube
options.note: v1; 19:7a and 55:10's verb, where 'nunc' / 'ecce' mark a moment. Heard as news by two readers.

options.label: eu reconheci
options.note: The stylist (v1): a confession. recognóscere's cognate.

options.label: eu conheci
options.note: MS1932; DRB 'I have known'. The stylist refused 'conheci que' at 55:10.

decisions.why: Two verbs of bringing stand in one verse: edúcens nubes and prodúcit ventos, both 'lead forth, bring out' in L&S. v1 took edúcere from its Greek (ἀνάγων, 'faz subir') and gave 'fazer sair' to prodúcere; the Latinist (v1, minor) objected that 'faz subir' follows the LXX, not the Latin verb (rule 1). v2: edúcere keeps its row ('fazer sair', 17:20) and the Latin's sense, the clouds brought out from the end of the earth; prodúcere, to stay apart in the same verse, takes 'tirar' — 'Tira dos seus depósitos os ventos', the verb of the Diurnal Monástico ('tira o vento dos cofres', DM1962 — borrowed for diction only). The participle is a finite verb (D2 grammar); the subject is the Lord of 134:6.

options.label: Faz sair … Tira
options.note: v2 ruling. The Latinist's 'Faz sair' (the edúcere row); 'Tira' for prodúcere after DM1962.

options.label: Faz subir … Faz sair
options.note: v1. ἀνάγων / ἐξάγων; MS1932 'faz subir … faz sair'. The Latinist: LXX, not the Latin.

options.label: Fazendo sair … Aquele que tira
options.note: The Latin's participle and relative kept (103:14's gerund, 113:8's 'Aquele que').

decisions.why: ἀστραπὰς εἰς ὑετὸν ἐποίησεν: 'made lightnings for the rain' (DRB) — lightning that goes with, or turns into, the rain. 'para a chuva' keeps the verb 'fez' and the purpose/direction of 'in' without deciding the physics. MS1932 'converte os relâmpagos em chuva' replaces the verb with 'converter' and decides 'into'. The perfect 'fecit' is kept after the present of the first colon, as the Latin shifts tense.

options.label: fez relâmpagos para a chuva
options.note: Ruling. The Latin's verb; DRB 'he hath made lightnings for the rain'.

options.label: fez dos relâmpagos chuva
options.note: 'in' read as 'into' (the pónere + two accusatives build of 104:32, 'Fez das chuvas deles granizo').

options.label: converteu os relâmpagos em chuva
options.note: MS1932 (present 'converte'); another verb, decides the sense.

decisions.why: thesáurus → depósito is the row (32:7 'põe em depósitos os abismos'), which names this verse: θησαυροί are storehouses, and 'tesouros' was heard as riches. The row asks to keep the proparoxytone off a cadence, so the object moves after it: 'faz sair dos seus depósitos os ventos' (order, D2), and the mediant falls on 'ventos'. MS1932 'dos seus tesouros' is the option. v2: the stylist asked 'tesouros' (depósitos 'commercial'), and the ambiguity reader found 'depósitos' odd as God's storehouses. Held for the row (open; 32:7 already reads 'depósitos', and 'tesouros' was heard as riches there by two readers); 'tesouros' stays the option, for Gustavo with the row.

options.label: dos seus depósitos
options.note: Ruling. The row (32:7).

options.label: dos seus tesouros
options.note: MS1932; the stylist (v1). Heard as riches at 32:7.

decisions.latin: Qui prodúcit … qui percússit … Qui percússit
decisions.why: From 134:7a the psalm is a chain of participles and relatives hanging on 'Dóminus' of 134:6 (Edúcens … Qui prodúcit … qui percússit … Qui percússit … et dedit). A Portuguese verse that opens on a bare relative has no main verb anywhere; the chain is made of main clauses, the Lord as subject throughout, named ('Ele') where a new sentence begins after the Egypt verse — grammar (D2). 113:8 kept 'Aquele que converteu', a single relative; here there are three in four verses. The relative chain ('Aquele que … que feriu … Aquele que feriu') is the option.

options.label: feriu … Ele feriu
options.note: Ruling. Main clauses; the subject carried from 134:6–7a and named again at 134:10, after the Egypt verse. (The head of 134:7b is in decision educens.)

options.label: ele feriu … Ele feriu
options.note: The subject named in 134:7b too (+2 syllables). The ambiguity reader could briefly attach 'feriu' to the winds; the singular verb against plural 'ventos' prevents it grammatically.

options.label: que feriu … Aquele que feriu
options.note: The Latin's relatives kept (113:8's build).

decisions.why: pecus (κτήνους) is the livestock; the row 'oves / boves / pécora' (open) names this place and gives 'animais'; juménta is 'animais' too (77:48, 106:38). The singular is kept, as a pair with 'o homem'. 'gado' is the row's narrower option. v2: both the Latinist and the stylist asked 'gado'; taken — the concrete word (rule 5).

options.label: gado
options.note: v2 ruling: the Latinist and the stylist (v1, both) — pecus is livestock, and 'animal' made the concrete word generic. The row's narrower option; DRB 'beast'.

options.label: animal
options.note: v1; the row 'pécora → animais'; MS1932 'até ao animal'.

decisions.latin: in Pharaónem, et in omnes servos ejus
decisions.why: in + accusative, ἐν Φαραω: the signs were sent upon Pharaoh. 'sobre' keeps the direction without naming hostility; MS1932 has 'contra'. 'Faraó' without an article, as a name (MS1932, DM1962). 'in … et in' is kept as a repeated preposition.

options.label: sobre Faraó e sobre
options.note: Ruling. DRB 'upon Pharao, and upon'.

decisions.why: Proper names take their current Brazilian form: Basã (67:23), Canaã (104:11, 105:38) are settled in earlier psalms; 'amorreus' lower case as a people. For Sehon, 'Seon' is what circulates — MS1932 and the CNBB Liturgia das Horas ('A Seon que foi rei amorreu', fetched, circulation.md). The Latin's spelling 'Sehon' (DRB) is the option. Ps 135:19–20 has the same two kings and should use the same forms (proposed in glossary.md).

options.label: Seon
options.note: Ruling. MS1932; CNBB LH.

options.label: Sehon
options.note: The Latin's spelling; DRB.

decisions.why: The Greek is παρακληθήσεται ἐπὶ τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ, the same verb and preposition as 89:13 'deprecábilis esto super servos tuos' (παρακλήθητι ἐπὶ τοὺς δούλους σου), which reads 'deixai-vos aplacar para com os vossos servos' (row 'deprecábilis', open). The Latin passive of deprecári is 'will let himself be entreated' (DRB 'will be entreated in favour of his servants'); 'deixar-se aplacar' is that, and rule 6 wants the two verses kin. This colon is sung alone at the end of the Tuesday Lauds antiphon ([Day2 Laudes2]: 'Laudáte Dóminum quia benígnus est, et in servis suis deprecábitur') and reads alone. Natural order (verb before its complement) over the Latin's verb-last. Costs: 'aplacar' was listed unknown by one reader at 89:13; the link with deprecári → suplicar (D35) is lost, as there. v2: the stylist (v1) named this colon the worst line — 'aplacar para com' lumpy, breath out before the cadence; the ambiguity reader listed 'aplacar' unknown and was unsure what it meant; the Latinist (minor) found 'aplacar' leans to propitiation and asked 'se deixará rogar'. Refused: in Brazil 'deixar-se rogar' / 'fazer-se rogar' is heard as making oneself be begged (reluctance), the opposite of the sense; and it would split this verse from 89:13, same Greek. Taken in part from the stylist: the Latin's own order, verb last — the preposition early while there is breath, the colon closing on the stressed '-car'. His 'com os seus servos' (dropping 'para') is refused: 'aplacar-se com' is heard as 'appeased by' them. The words stay 89:13's; if 89:13 changes, this follows.

options.label: e para com os seus servos se deixará aplacar

forms.deprec: e para com os seus servos se deixará aplacar

options.note: v2 ruling. The Latin's order (stylist, in part); 89:13's words.

forms.deprec: e se deixará vencer pelas preces dos seus servos

forms.deprec: e terá compaixão dos seus servos

decisions.why: 134:15 is 113:12 word for word; it copies 113:12 (rule 6; simulácrum row: 'ídolo', εἴδωλα). If 113:12 changes, this changes with it. v2: the Latinist asked 'simulacros' (minor), as he did at 113:12; refused for the same reason, and to keep the twins identical.

options.label: ídolos

options.label: simulacros

decisions.latin: neque enim est spíritus in ore ipsórum
decisions.why: The one colon of the idol-stanza not shared with Ps 113. spíritus is breath here (the spíritus row 'sopro', 102:16: wind and breath; 'espírito' would be heard as a soul). 'neque enim' = 'for there is not even': 'pois nem há' renders both words. 'sua' for ipsórum, as 113:15. MS1932 'porque não há alento de vida na sua boca' adds 'de vida'. v2: the stylist (v1) heard 'nem há' as a clipped calque and asked 'nem sequer'; taken — it is how Portuguese says 'not even', and renders neque's force better (grammar, D2). His 'em sua boca' is not taken: the article before the possessive (rule 5).

decisions.latin: Símiles illis fiant qui fáciunt ea
decisions.why: 134:18 is 113:16 word for word; it copies 113:16 v2 (decision 'fiant' there: 'Façam-se' keeps the fiant / fáciunt play; 'aqueles que' avoids 'os que os'). v2: the stylist asked 'Tornem-se … os que os fazem' (the 'Façam-se … fazem' jingle, 'a eles aqueles'); refused: the echo is the Latin's fiant / fáciunt, and 113:16 made the same ruling against the same proposal; 'Tornem-se' stays option 2.

options.label: Façam-se
options.note: Ruling, = 113:16.

options.label: Tornem-se

options.label: Sejam
options.note: MS1932; loses the becoming.

decisions.latin: Benedíctus Dóminus ex Sion, * qui hábitat in Jerúsalem.
decisions.why: 'Benedíctus Dóminus' is verbless 'Bendito o Senhor' in every finished place (27:6, 30:22, 67:20, 123:6 …). 133:3 has 'ex Sion → de Sião', but 'Bendito o Senhor de Sião' is heard as 'the Lord of Zion'; 'desde Sião' (MS1932) says the place the blessing comes from. The relative is given 'ele', as 133:3 does, because it would otherwise attach to 'Sião'. MS1932's order ('Desde Sião seja bendito o Senhor, que habita…') lets the relative follow 'Senhor' directly, but supplies 'seja' against the formula.

options.label: Bendito o Senhor desde Sião, * ele que habita em Jerusalém.

decisions.why: The memoriále row (open) asks 134:13 to copy 101:13 ('e o vosso memorial, de geração em geração'). The stylist (v1) heard 'memorial' as a monument or legal brief and asked 'memória'; the ambiguity reader listed it unknown but heard 'remembrance'. Held for rule 6 (101:13 is the same colon; μνημόσυνον, which in the Greek is the memorial name by which God is remembered and invoked — not the faculty 'memória', which 29:5 already uses for memória). 'a vossa memória' is the option, for Gustavo with the row.

options.label: o vosso memorial
options.note: Ruling; = 101:13.

options.label: a vossa memória
options.note: The stylist (v1); MS1932 'a tua memória'.

choices.134:1: The Alleluia title (LXX αλληλουια; MS1932 prints 'Aleluia.') is not in DO's Latin, which opens on 'Laudáte nomen Dómini'; as in Pss 110–113 it is not reproduced (D7). 'Louvai, servos, o Senhor': 112:1's build ('Louvai, meninos, o Senhor'), the vocative bare. 'Senhor … Senhor' at mediant and final is the Latin's own echo (Dómini / Dóminum). The first colon is sung alone as an antiphon ([Day2 Laudes1]). The checks flag the rhyme Senhor / Senhor: it is the Latin's Dómini / Dóminum, kept (as 134:19–20 keep Dómino / Dómino, and 134:16 falarão / verão = 113:13, the Latin's loquéntur / vidébunt).
choices.134:2: Otherwise 133:1b word for word (stare → estar de pé; átrium → átrio). See decision statis. +3 syllables on the first colon (the named 'Vós' and 'de pé'), accepted.
choices.134:3: quia / quóniam both → porque. 'quóniam suáve' (neuter; ὅτι καλόν): what is sweet may be the name (nomen is neuter) or the singing; 'porque é suave' keeps it open. suávis → suave (row, 99:4b). psállere → entoar salmos (D25).
choices.134:4: The verb and subject brought forward (natural order, D2); Jacó at the mediant. 'in possessiónem sibi' → 'como sua posse' after 32:12 'quem elégit in hereditátem sibi → que ele escolheu como sua herança' (sibi absorbed into the possessive). heréditas / posséssio → herança / posse (row). περιουσιασμός is a treasured possession; 'posse' is the row's word for the land (2:8).
choices.134:5: præ ómnibus diis → acima de todos os deuses (95:4 'acima de todos os deuses', 88:28 præ → acima de). The second colon is verbless as the Latin's.
choices.134:6: Its head copies 113:11's 'tudo o que quis, ele fez' with Dóminus named, as the glossary's 113:11 note asks; the antiphon 'Tudo o que quis, o Senhor fez' ([Daya4 Vespera], [Monastic Vespera] feria 4) reads alone. The first colon is short against the Latin (≈13 vs 20 syllables): Portuguese uses fewer. (checks: −6)
choices.134:7a: ab extrémo terræ → do extremo da terra (the CNBB LH has the same words, fetched). See decisions educens and fulgura. The ambiguity reader noticed the tense shift (Faz … fez), which is the Latin's (Edúcens … fecit), and still heard what God does; kept.
choices.134:7b: DO's (8) run in, not reproduced. primogénita → os primogênitos (77:51). See decisions educens (Tira), thesauris, qui, pecus.
choices.134:9: mittere → enviar (56:4b). signa et prodígia → sinais e prodígios (77:43, 104:27). The vocative 'Egito' without 'ó' (the psalter's rule: 'ó' only where the Latin has 'o').
choices.134:10: gentes multas → muitas nações (plainer than 96:1's 'numerosas'). reges fortes → reis fortes (fortes row: strong or mighty, open as the Latin; 135:18 has the same words).
choices.134:12: The Latin repeats 'hereditátem', and the Portuguese repeats 'como herança'. 'pópulo suo' → 'o seu povo', the article before the possessive.
choices.134:13: The second colon copies 101:13b ('e o vosso memorial, de geração em geração'), as the memoriále row asks; the copula supplied in the first ('é para sempre', D14's build) and understood in the second. in ætérnum → para sempre (D23). The second colon is 7 syllables short of the Latin (checks): 'de geração em geração' is the formula.
choices.134:14: judicáre → julgar (row). The second colon is +4 (checks): 89:13's phrase costs it.
choices.134:16: = 113:13 word for word; the Latin's futures kept, as there.
choices.134:17: The first colon = 113:14a. Ps 113 has two more pairs (nose, hands, feet); Ps 134 has not.
choices.134:19: benedícere + dative → 'bendizei ao Senhor' (row; 102:20–22, 113:26). Aaron → Aarão.
choices.134:20: 'qui timétis Dóminum' → 'vós que temeis o Senhor' (21:24).
choices.134:18: = 113:16 word for word (v2 there); +4 syllables on the first colon, as there.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps134.md, with ps113 (idols), ps133 (133:1b = 134:2; 133:3 ex Sion), 89:13 (deprecábilis, same Greek as 134:14), 101:13 (memoriále), 19:7a / 55:10 (cognóvi + clause) as precedents. Liturgical uses by grep (three antiphons) and Brazilian circulation (CNBB LH, fetched) in circulation.md. Hard readings: 134:14 deprecábitur, 134:7a fúlgura in plúviam, 134:2 against its formula.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 134:7a +4 and 134:7b second colon +5 in the first run — mended by leaving the subject unnamed ('Faz subir', 'Faz sair … feriu'), now within range; 134:17 'boca deles' rhymed with 134:18 'neles' — mended ('na sua boca', as 113:15). Accepted: 134:2 +3, 134:5 +3 ('acima de' for præ), 134:14 +4 (89:13's phrase), 134:18 +4 (= 113:16), 134:6 −6 and 134:13 −7 (Portuguese is shorter; the formula); the Senhor/Senhor, Dómino/Dómino echoes of 134:1, 19, 20 and falarão/verão of 134:16 are the Latin's.
No critical or major; 4 minor. 2 taken (7a Faz sair; 7b gado), 2 refused (14 rogar; 15 simulacros).

Kept: 134:3 owner of 'suave' open (the Latin's neuter); 7a 'para a chuva' heard as accompanying (the Latin's 'in' left open); 7b 'feriu' briefly attachable to the winds (verb singular, ventos plural); 14 'julgará' with an overtone of condemnation (the Latin's word); 14 'aplacar' unclear (held with 89:13; order changed); proper names and átrio kept (the Latin's; rows).
